reasons.A: Measured, formal, hedged ('I suspect', 'perhaps') with some long sentences, but it has more short declaratives, no rhetorical questions and less semicolon linking than the author's long, flowing sentences.
reasons.B: Closest match: it opens with a question, uses long multi-clause sentences joined by semicolons, and has the same reflective hedging ('arguably', 'I suspect', 'perhaps') and the same questions put to the reader. 'Who among us' leans slightly towards caricature.
reasons.C: Short, punchy, plain sentences with a blunt, assertive tone and a problem-and-fix ending; the rhythm and stance are far from the author's long, hedged, reflective periods.
